page.layout: One printed page (page 50). Running head at top centre above the text. Main text in one column, with indented lines and italic headings-like lines in the body. Two-column passage in the middle (left list and right list, "Aër frigidus" / "Balneum frigidum", etc.). Show-through from the reverse page appears faintly on the right and is omitted.

main_text.p: In quibus recens aliqua, quæ externa sit, alteratio:

p.i: Victoriam motus illius, cui pulsus magnus est peculiaris.

main_text.p: Minorem solito citra facultatis imbecillitatem, & arteriæ duritiam parit:

p.i: Quæ intrò recipiuntur: vt aër, cibus pituito sus, frigida vsus immodicus.
Pulsuum igitur in magnitudine, & paruita te mu-

page.notes: The left margin of the page is blank. Faint show-through from the facing page is not transcribed. The line "Vsus remissionem," and the lists are printed as given; "Balneum frigidum" and "Medicamentum inunctum" are in the right column of the two-column list. "te mu-" at the foot is a catchword-like continuation word placed at the right; it is recorded here as the line end of the last paragraph.
